scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 0.88 against a 0.95 target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL (billing-db).

F-03.statement: Dispute response times: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, across 2440 tickets (crm-tickets).

F-04.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log returned 0 records for the period, i.e. no logged tariff change.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 states the utility may request route priority changes, which are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log lagging_routes returned 14 routes with distinct completion values (sample: route R-00 completion=0.70), i.e. per-route detail beneath the Aug-Sep aggregate 0.88 completion rate (E-01).

F-08.statement: billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle returned 320 records (fields account_id, route) with 320 distinct account_id values and 40 distinct route values; sample {account_id: AC-20000, route: R-00}.

F-09.statement: mdms-export read_events_for_disputed_estimated returned 2 records: 1184 AMI reads received before cutoff but rejected at billing import (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, exported_to_billing=true, firmware v4.2); 56 with no read received (NO_READ_RECEIVED, exported_to_billing=false).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-TICKET-RESPONSE-LATENCY.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a customer-service response/handling bottleneck rather than a bill-accuracy defect, so an auto-answer agent as SH-CS requests would resolve it.

H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI/MDMS read export delivery or validity degraded around August, producing estimated or incorrect reads that flowed into wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: Manual field meter-read delivery or quality degraded around August (e.g. incomplete routes), causing more estimate substitutions and wrong bills.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules introduced around August caused reads to be mis-validated or wrongly estimated, generating incorrect bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Reduced field reading staffing capacity (per SH-FIELD's framing) led to incomplete read routes, more missed reads, and more estimate-driven wrong bills.

H-BILLING-CALC-ERROR.statement: A substantial share of disputed bills (1785, 59%) carry ACTUAL read type, suggesting wrong bills can arise downstream of read acquisition — e.g. billing calculation or tariff application errors on accepted reads — not only from estimate substitution.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT.statement: Billing import rejects valid AMI reads flagged as high consumption (status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) and substitutes an estimate instead, accounting for 1184 of 1240 (95%) ESTIMATED-type disputed bills, independent of field route completion or AMI delivery issues.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log record shows manual-read route completion ran at 0.88 against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts over Aug-Sep 2026, confirming a real but moderate shortfall in field manual read delivery during the dispute-surge period, rather than full route completion as planned.

Of 3025 total disputed bills, 1240 (41%) are ESTIMATED-read-type and 1785 (59%) are ACTUAL-read-type, meaning most disputed bills involve accepted actual reads, not estimate substitutions. This indicates estimate-substitution mechanisms (missed/failed reads) account for only a minority of the dispute symptom.

The crm-tickets dispute_response_times record shows a 1.6-day median and 2.8-day p90 response time against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, i.e. ticket handling is currently meeting the SLA rather than breaching it.

The billing-db tariff_change_log returned zero records, meaning no tariff change was logged for the period, ruling out a tariff-rate change as the mechanism behind the wrong bills on ACTUAL-read disputes.

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly shows 610 (Jun), 590 (Jul), 1180 (Aug), 1260 (Sep) 2026, confirming ticket volume roughly doubled starting in August (1180/590≈2.0x) and remained elevated in September. This quantifies the magnitude/timing of the surge but says nothing about its mechanism or cause.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that no tariff change occurred this year is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that corroborates the already-recorded authoritative finding (E-04: billing-db tariff_change_log, 0 records). It adds no new data and does not expand the ruled-out mechanism beyond what E-04 already established.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a three-reader staffing shortfall since July causes late routes and resulting estimated bills, offering a causal story for the route-completion shortfall already quantified in E-01/F-01. This is a non-authoritative, incomplete stakeholder claim from a party with a disclosed incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias toward staffing attribution, not new measured data.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: This authoritative contract document confirms the existing K-DISPATCH authority structure: the utility may request field route priority changes, but execution requires Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) confirmation. It does not speak to the billing dispute surge's root cause and is unrelated to the read-type/rule-change causal chain.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log lagging_routes returned per-route completion detail for 14 routes (sample: R-00=0.70), showing the Aug-Sep aggregate 0.88 completion figure (E-01) masks route-level variance. This supplies only the field-side half of the planned join against billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle needed to address U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION; the join itself has not yet been run.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) returns 320 accounts that received estimated bills last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (sample AC-20000/R-00). This is the billing-side half of the planned join against route-log per-route completion detail (E-09, 14 routes) needed to test U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION; the join itself (W-ANALYZE-ROUTE-COMPLETION-DET) has not yet been run, so no causal conclusion can be drawn from this record alone.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (vendor-side engineer) states MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today per vendor ticket TX-4471. This is a non-authoritative stakeholder message, not a tool confirmation; it claims the mdms-export access block may be lifted but supplies no actual AMI read-event data to test the AMI delivery hypothesis.

For the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills, mdms-export shows 1184 (95%) actually had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but rejected at import with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION; only 56 (5%) truly had NO_READ_RECEIVED. The dominant estimate-substitution mechanism is therefore a billing-import rejection of valid high-consumption AMI reads, not AMI delivery failure or field-side missed reads.

U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.question: Did a billing import validation rule change actually take effect around August, and does its pattern match the ACTUAL-read disputed accounts?
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.decision_impact: Confirms or falsifies the primary candidate mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE); if not found, the billing-defect hypothesis must be revisited via calculation-logic review (H-BILLING-CALC-ERROR).
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule change log (DA-RULES) for entries dated around August and cross-reference with disputed ACTUAL-read account IDs.
U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED.safe_placeholder: Do not attribute or remediate any specific rule change until the log is reviewed; continue read-only investigation only.

U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.question: Is AMI/MDMS read delivery or validity degraded, contributing to wrong actual-reads, given mdms-export is currently DEGRADED and access is ACCESS_PENDING?
U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.decision_impact: If AMI delivery is also degraded, remediation scope would need to extend to ORG-AMI vendor coordination, not just billing-side config, per H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE.
U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.resolution_path: ORG-AMI vendor must provision mdms-export access (per DA-MDMS acquisition note); current retry is blocked by a logged NOT_TRANSIENT hold.
U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-side investigation using already-accessible billing-db/billing-config/route-log data; treat the AMI mechanism as unresolved.
U-AMI-EXPORT-ACCESS-BLOCKED.resolution: AMI delivery is largely NOT degraded: 1184/1240 (95%) ESTIMATED-disputed accounts had an AMI read received before cutoff and successfully exported to billing; the failure point is billing import rejection (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), not AMI read delivery itself. Only 56 lacked a received read.

U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.question: Does raw dispute ticket volume (G-1) adequately measure success, or could an auto-answer agent (CL-01) reduce ticket counts without fixing underlying bill accuracy?
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Determines whether a response-handling solution as SH-CS requested would satisfy G-1 despite not fixing the root billing defect; a separate bill-accuracy metric is needed.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Define and track a bill-accuracy rate (corrected bills / total disputed bills) alongside raw ticket volume.
U-SUCCESS-METRIC-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Track both dispute-volume trend and bill-accuracy rate; do not close the problem on ticket-count reduction alone.

U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does the 0.88 vs 0.95 route-completion shortfall (9200 accounts) fully explain the 41% ESTIMATED-type disputes, or is there an independent estimate-substitution defect?
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether field-side remediation (route completion improvement, possibly a push_route_update under K-DISPATCH) is needed alongside the billing-side fix.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Cross-reference ESTIMATED-type disputed accounts against route-log completion records for the same period.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Treat field route shortfall as a secondary, unconfirmed contributor; do not propose route-dispatch changes until confirmed.
U-FIELD-SHORTFALL-CONTRIBUTION.resolution: Yes, an independent estimate-substitution defect exists: billing import rejects valid high-consumption AMI reads (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) for 1184/1240 ESTIMATED-disputed bills, a mechanism independent of the field route-completion shortfall.

A-DISPUTED-BILL-PROXY.statement: Disputed bill counts (E-02) are assumed to reasonably proxy actual wrong-bill incidence rather than reflecting duplicate or non-substantive disputes.

A-RULES-LOG-COMPLETENESS.statement: The billing import validation rule change log (DA-RULES) is assumed complete enough to reveal an August change if one occurred, though its completeness is marked UNKNOWN.

A-SURGE-WINDOW-ALIGNMENT.statement: The Aug-Sep route-completion shortfall (E-01) is assumed to temporally and account-wise overlap with the dispute surge window, though this has not been directly cross-referenced.

A-BASELINE-REPRESENTATIVENESS.statement: Jun-Jul ticket counts (610, 590) are assumed to represent a normal, non-seasonal baseline for comparison against the Aug-Sep surge.

Both wrong actual-read bills and wrong estimated bills are issued to customers via the normal bill-issue step of meter-to-cash (P-M2C).
Customers receiving incorrect bills open dispute tickets in the CRM.
Monthly dispute ticket counts roughly double from ~600 (Jun/Jul baseline) to ~1180-1260 (Aug/Sep) (F-05/E-05).

Tariff-rate change and dispute-response latency are ruled out as mechanisms (F-04/E-04 zero tariff changes logged; F-03/E-03 response times within SLA), narrowing the surge's cause to upstream bill-accuracy defects rather than service handling.

proposal.summary: SH-CS asked for an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and 'fix whatever is causing the wrong bills' (CL-01). Investigation established the real problem is not slow ticket handling but a bill-accuracy defect: dispute volume roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep (F-05/E-05), and 59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) carry an ACTUAL (accepted) read type versus 41% ESTIMATED (F-02/E-02), meaning most wrong bills arise downstream of read acquisition rather than from missed/estimated reads. Tariff change was ruled out (F-04/E-04) and ticket response times are within SLA (F-03/E-03), so the SH-CS framing of a response-speed problem (H-TICKET-RESPONSE-LATENCY) was rejected. A deeper look at the ESTIMATED share (E-12) found 95% of those bills (1184/1240) actually had valid AMI reads received but rejected at billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, pointing to a billing-import validation defect (H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT, H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE) rather than field or AMI delivery failure, which also led to rejecting H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION: the DEFINE gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, and the release is scoped to the two feasible, low-risk work items (route-completion detail analysis on DA-ROUTE and dispute-ticket-volume monitoring on DA-TICKET), while confirming and fixing the actual billing rule defect, writing bill adjustments, and pushing route changes are out of scope because they are blocked, infeasible in contest time, and/or require protected authorizations (K-BILLWRITE, K-DISPATCH) that were not exercised.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS) framed the surge as a response-handling problem needing an AI auto-answer agent; this framing was tested and rejected (H-TICKET-RESPONSE-LATENCY) because response times are within SLA (F-03/E-03) and the shortfall is route-completion not latency (F-01/E-01).

Dispute volume doubling (F-05/E-05) and the 59%/41% ACTUAL vs ESTIMATED split (F-02/E-02) show most wrong bills come from a billing-import defect on accepted reads, not simple estimate substitution; tariff change was ruled out (F-04/E-04).

E-12 shows 95% (1184/1240) of ESTIMATED disputed bills actually had valid AMI reads received before cutoff but rejected at import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, supporting H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-REJECT/H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE and rejecting H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE and H-AMI-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE as the dominant mechanism.

The release scope was limited to analyze_route_completion_detail:DA-ROUTE and monitor_dispute_ticket_volume:DA-TICKET (solution_design release_scope), both read-only/monitoring actions; no automated bill writes (K-BILLWRITE) or route pushes (K-DISPATCH) were performed, consistent with those protected-action constraints.

Decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION reflects that the DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with deferred items tracked as open verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved before release.
